architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

core_scientific_tool.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
core_scientific_tool.role: Convert the paper's upstream findings into machine-usable design rules without exposing the validation formulation or its outcome.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities
reproducibility of the recommendation under the same evidence contract
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

acceptance_criterion.claim: S1C41 mitigates the established thermal-hold viscosity instability while retaining an interpretable 80-130 °C response and repeatability comparable to the characterized local realization spread.
acceptance_criterion.criterion: Under the matched 120 °C hold protocol, SI15-60 must be below 0.515 and SI15-90 must be below 0.931, with the complete 15, 60, and 90 minute trajectory recorded. The 80-130 °C response must remain monotonic decreasing and descriptively interpretable after state calibration. Repeated realizations must have CV no greater than 0.58 and maximum/minimum ratio no greater than 3.6, with complete stoichiometric, modifier-functionality, process-history, and state records.
acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Failure occurs if either SI threshold is not improved relative to E5, if the trajectory or required baseline is incomplete, if the response is non-monotonic or uninterpretable, if repeatability exceeds either frozen limit, if stoichiometry or modifier functionality cannot be verified, or if process/state records are insufficient to distinguish formulation effects from realization-state variation.
acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: Repeated temperature sweeps over 80-130 °C; matched thermal hold at 120 °C with measurements at 15, 60, and 90 minutes. The 15-minute pre-hold measurement is the SI baseline; the separate 120 °C state anchor must be collected and documented without changing the hold trajectory.

alternatives_considered.relative_reason: Covers both supported axes with lower modifier burden, but its 2.5% tackifier level is below the stated evidence-supported 3-10% region and below the repeated 4.8-6.4% analogue cluster; the robustness objection therefore defeats its minimum-burden advantage.
Provides a justified acrylic-loading robustness point, but retains the less-supported 2.5% tackifier level and has a higher total modifier burden than S1C41.
Useful as a tackifier-only mechanistic control, but it zeroes the independently supported acrylic axis and is not an adequate default performance-mitigation experiment.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: The primary failure mode is thermal-hold viscosity instability, not merely static viscosity or temperature dependence. Local experiments show a large matched-hold contrast between E1 and E5, while E2 shows substantial realization/process-state spread. The state-aware rheology rule therefore requires formulation plus process state, one in-range state calibration anchor, and direct hold testing; the formulation-only response is not sufficient. The local measurements and rheological rules support preserving the E2 reactive core and measuring both temperature response and temporal drift. Curated PUR literature/database evidence supports an acrylic-like modifier family in a broad 15-25% region and a minor tackifier region centered near 5%, but these priors are analogue and directional rather than predictors of the held-out wet-lab result. S1C41 is selected because it covers both independently supported intervention axes for the declared performance-mitigation intent, uses 15% acrylic-like modifier and 5% tackifier-like modifier within the stated evidence regions, and avoids the unsupported 2.5% tackifier extrapolation in S1C40. The minimum-sufficient-intervention principle is applied only after coverage and loading sufficiency: S1C41 is preferred over higher-burden full-coverage candidates, not because it is closest to a literature point. The Skeptic's objections are resolved by replacing S1C40, freezing repeatability and temperature-response limits, requiring comparison with both E5 failure and E1 low-drift references, verifying modifier functionality and stoichiometry, and defining state-anchor timing separately from the SI baseline. The Robustness Adjudicator's objection is resolved by selecting its supported full-coverage alternative S1C41. The decision supports a bounded formulation region and a falsifiable experiment, not an exact property prediction or molecular mechanism.

action_requests.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
action_requests.reason: Required first to obtain the upstream formulation-only versus state-aware comparison, state-shift master-curve structure, one-point calibration result, local temperature-sensitivity coordinate, E1/E5 hold-drift contrast, and the measurement rules that determine whether state calibration or temporal stability should dominate candidate adjudication.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: After the local objective and failure mode are established, retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, E2 reactive-core anchor, independently supported acrylic and tackifier axes, and historical/claim boundary before comparing candidate regions.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Thermal-hold stability at 120 °C over the measured 15-90 min window, using SI and absolute drift.
Viscosity level at an anchor temperature within the measured 80-130 °C support, without treating a single nominal value as definitive.
Temperature-response shape and local apparent temperature sensitivity over the supported sweep.
State-aware versus formulation-only predictability and need for one-point state calibration.
Repeatability and realization/process-state spread, including run-to-run CV and max/min ratio.
Compatibility with the original E2 reactive-core anchor and explicit stoichiometric balance.
Acrylic modifier fraction and modifier functionality as separate considerations.
Minor tackifier fraction and identity as a separate intervention axis.
Evidence directness: directly commensurate numeric anchors versus directional/noncommensurate analogue evidence.
Extrapolation distance from local measured chemistry, temperature, time, and process-history support.
Feasibility and processability risks introduced by the combined modifier loading.
counterfactual_checks: Would the candidate still be preferred if its nominal viscosity level were shifted by the observed E2 repeat/run spread?
Would the candidate still be preferred if state calibration were omitted or if the formulation-only model were used?
Does the candidate reduce thermal-hold drift relative to the E5 high-drift reference without merely moving to an unsupported viscosity or temperature region?
Is the apparent benefit attributable to the acrylic axis, the tackifier axis, their combination, or unresolved process-state differences?
Would an E2-core-only or single-axis alternative provide comparable hold stability with lower extrapolation and attribution risk?
Does the candidate remain within the bounded acrylic and tackifier regions supported by pre-result evidence rather than relying on an inferred exact optimum?
Could the apparent improvement be explained by a change in realization/process state rather than chemistry?
If hold stability improves but temperature sensitivity or repeatability worsens, is that tradeoff acceptable under the frozen decision objective?
Would the decision change if directional literature evidence were removed while retaining only locally measured rheology and directly commensurate anchors?
Can the candidate's outcome be adjudicated using the prespecified measurements without inspecting or invoking the held-out validation formulation or outcome?
planner.decision_goal: Select one pre-result candidate experiment that mitigates the established thermal-hold viscosity-drift failure while preserving an interpretable viscosity-temperature response and explicitly accounting for substantial realization/process-state uncertainty.
design_implications: Optimize measured hold-drift behavior, not only a nominal viscosity at one temperature.
Keep the candidate within the measured temperature domain or use 80-130 °C as the supported anchor range; do not infer performance outside that range without new evidence.
Use the original E2 reactive core as the reference unless the candidate hypothesis identifies a specifically justified formulation-family change.

A multi-component intervention is admissible in performance-mitigation mode when the acrylic and tackifier axes are independently supported and remain within bounded pre-result evidence-supported regions.
Prefer a bounded acrylic-modifier region centered on the externally supported coarse range rather than treating 15%, 20%, or 25% as an exact optimum.
Treat a minor tackifier axis as an optional, bounded stability/processability intervention rather than silently fixing it at zero or interpreting its literature percentage as a local optimum.
Use the state-shift master-curve result from the upstream summary to decide whether one-point state calibration is required before comparing candidates.
Use the distinct thermal-versus-temporal response result from the upstream summary to ensure the next experiment measures both temperature response and time-dependent hold drift.
Preserve unknown viscosity units and source units; do not convert or compare absolute viscosity values across sources unless commensurability is established.
Keep process history, stoichiometric balance, modifier functionality, and realization uncertainty explicit during candidate comparison.
Do not claim a molecular mechanism from the rheology evidence alone.
material_regularities_to_use: Measured temperature sweeps for E1, E2, and E3 are monotonic decreasing over the supported 80-130 °C range.
Temperature-response curves are descriptively well represented by Andrade-type fits, but the fit parameters vary across runs and formulations.
E2 is the original reactive-core anchor and has substantial nominal repeat/run spread, so viscosity level must be evaluated together with realization/process-state uncertainty.
The original thermal-hold comparison establishes a large stability contrast at 120 °C over the measured 15-90 min window: E1 is low-drift and E5 is high-drift.
Thermal response, thermal-hold stability, nominal viscosity level, and realization/process state are separate decision dimensions.
The candidate lattice is pre-result and supports regional or directional recovery only; candidate IDs do not encode rank and do not identify the held-out formulation.
External acrylic evidence provides coarse anchors near 15%, 20%, and 25% total formulation, while tackifier evidence supports a minor-modifier axis up to about 10%; these are not exact local optima.
The low-OH versus higher-OH acrylic comparison is directional comparative-stability evidence, not proof of the local mechanism or a transferable exact loading.
planner.physical_failure_mode: Thermal-hold instability is the primary established failure mode: at 120 °C, E5 shows large viscosity rise (SI=0.515 from 15 to 60 min and SI=0.931 from 15 to 90 min), whereas E1 is substantially more stable (SI=0.095 and 0.168). This is distinct from the generally monotonic decrease in viscosity with temperature. Nominal viscosity is also not fully reliable as a material property because E2 has large within-temperature run spread, with CV approximately 0.46-0.58 and maximum/minimum ratios approximately 2.8-3.6.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: Temperature sweep over the supported 80-130 °C range for the selected candidate, with viscosity units and measurement conditions recorded.
At least repeated temperature-sweep runs sufficient to estimate descriptive run spread, CV, and maximum/minimum ratio.
Thermal-hold trajectory at 120 °C with measurements at 15, 60, and 90 min, or the same frozen local hold schedule used for the E1/E5 comparison.
SI=(eta_t1-eta_t0)/eta_t0 reported for 15-60 and 15-90 min, together with the underlying trajectory rather than SI alone.
A state or realization indicator and complete process-history record sufficient to determine whether observed differences are formulation-driven or state-driven.
One-point state calibration if the upstream summary confirms that state shifting materially improves the master-curve description.
Stoichiometric and composition verification, including reactive-core balance, acrylic fraction, tackifier fraction, and modifier functionality or OH-related descriptors where available.
Adjudication against viscosity level, temperature response, hold stability, repeatability, feasibility, and out-of-domain status using criteria frozen before result inspection.
uncertainty_triggers: The upstream summary shows a material state shift that is not represented by formulation composition alone.
A candidate's apparent improvement is smaller than the observed E2 realization/process-state spread.
The candidate requires temperature, time, or chemistry extrapolation beyond the measured support.
External evidence is only analogous or directional and is being used as if it were a directly commensurate numeric anchor.
Acrylic loading is selected from a literature percentage without accounting for different acrylic chemistry, functionality, molecular weight, catalysts, or process history.
Tackifier identity or loading changes simultaneously with acrylic loading without a predeclared rationale.
Hold data are incomplete, lack the 15 min baseline, or do not cover the local 15-90 min decision window.
Absolute viscosity comparisons rely on unknown or non-equivalent units.
Process history, stoichiometric balance, or candidate realization state is missing.
The candidate appears stable only because the measurement duration or temperature differs from the E1/E5 comparison.

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: The selected formulation-process point mitigates the established thermal-hold instability without an unacceptable loss of interpretable temperature response or repeatability.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.criterion: Under the matched 120 °C, 15-90 min protocol, both SI15-60 and SI15-90 must be lower than the corresponding E5 references of 0.515 and 0.931, respectively, with the complete trajectory recorded; the 80-130 °C response must remain monotonic decreasing and descriptive curve behavior must remain interpretable after state calibration.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Failure is declared if either hold-drift SI is not improved relative to the matched E5 reference, if the hold test lacks the 15 min baseline or complete 15-90 min window, if state/process records are insufficient to separate chemistry from realization state, or if the candidate shows non-interpretable temperature response or unacceptable run-to-run spread.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: 120 °C hold at 15, 60, and 90 min, plus repeated 80-130 °C temperature sweeps.

provisional_measurement_plan.primary_response: Matched thermal-hold viscosity trajectory at 120 °C with measurements at 15, 60, and 90 min; report SI15-60 and SI15-90 together with the underlying trajectory. Also measure repeated 80-130 °C temperature sweeps and quantify run spread, CV, maximum/minimum ratio, and descriptive temperature-response shape.
provisional_measurement_plan.state_anchor_plan: Control and document mixing history, reaction temperature/time, sample age, stoichiometric balance, modifier functionality, and realization identifiers. After equilibration, use one in-range viscosity anchor at 120 °C for each realization to calibrate the state shift before comparing temperature-response curves; do not use calibration as a substitute for the matched hold test.
provisional_measurement_plan.time_window: Temperature sweep: 80-130 °C. Thermal hold: 120 °C at 15, 60, and 90 min, matching the local E1/E5 comparison.

Measured local evidence: local temperature sweeps are monotonic decreasing over 80-130 °C and are descriptively represented by Andrade-type curves.
Measured local evidence: E2 has large realization/run spread, with CV approximately 0.46-0.58 and maximum/minimum ratios approximately 2.8-3.6.

Derived physical/model rule: realization state primarily shifts viscosity scale while a common temperature-response shape remains transferable; one in-range state anchor is therefore required for new realizations.
Derived physical/model rule: static viscosity, temperature response, and thermal-hold stability are separate responses; hold stability must be measured directly.

External analogue evidence: acrylic-like modifiers support a bounded family spanning approximately 15-25% total formulation, with approximately 19-20% directly commensurate examples and 15% retained as directional/noncommensurate lower-region evidence.
External analogue evidence: minor tackifier-like modifiers are directly commensurately represented near 4.8-6.4%, with broader directional guidance below about 10%.
Conservative design principle: preserve the E2 reactive-core proportions and compare full-coverage acrylic-plus-tackifier candidates before partial-coverage controls.

Unresolved uncertainty: external modifier chemistries, functionality, molecular weights, process histories, and reported viscosity units are not fully commensurate with AC1920/TK100 or the local system.
proposer.scientific_target: Mitigate thermal-hold viscosity instability at 120 °C while preserving an interpretable viscosity-temperature response and explicitly separating formulation effects from realization/process-state shifts.
unresolved_questions: Does the combined acrylic-like plus minor-tackifier intervention reduce true temporal hold drift rather than only shifting viscosity scale?
Is S1C40's lower modifier burden sufficient, or is the directly commensurate 5% tackifier level in S1C41 needed for robust improvement?
Does increasing acrylic loading from 15% to 17.5% materially change hold stability after state calibration?
What role do acrylic functionality, effective reactive-group density, and modifier identity play; current rheology does not establish a molecular mechanism.
Can process-history and realization-state control reduce uncertainty enough for candidate differences to exceed the observed E2 spread?
Are absolute viscosity values commensurate across all measurements and external sources; external numeric viscosity anchors should not be used as local acceptance targets.
The evidence supports a bounded formulation family and direction, not an exact optimum composition.

alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The tackifier loading must remain within the declared evidence-supported region and exact analogue-distance rewards are removed.

Record all available process-history and realization-state fields; declare the result uninterpretable if critical state information remains missing.

robustness_checks.detail: The proposal directly tests the established 120 °C thermal-hold viscosity-drift failure rather than relying on a nominal viscosity measurement.
The declared intent is performance_mitigation, so a dual-axis intervention is appropriate; causal-isolation single-axis controls should not replace the primary performance test.

robustness_checks.check: Coverage of independently supported intervention axes
robustness_checks.detail: S1C40 covers both axes but uses 2.5% tackifier, below the declared broad supported region of 3-10% and below the repeated 4.8-6.4% analogue cluster. Its minimum-burden rationale therefore depends on unsupported dose extrapolation.

robustness_checks.check: Robustness to removal of exact analogue-distance rewards
robustness_checks.detail: When evidence is treated as a supported region rather than an exact-distance objective, S1C41 is preferable because it retains full axis coverage with 15% acrylic and 5% tackifier, both within the declared supported regions.

One-point state calibration, matched hold testing, and process-history recording are appropriate, but all candidates have substantial missing process-state fields and modifier functionality may alter true NCO:OH balance.

The proposed 80-130 °C sweeps, repeated runs, and 120 °C measurements at 15, 60, and 90 minutes are sufficient in scope, but repeatability thresholds, tradeoff rules, state-anchor timing, and SI-baseline handling must be frozen before results.
The recommendation does not depend solely on analogue distance, but S1C40 depends materially on treating 2.5% tackifier as a valid low-burden intervention despite the stated evidence boundary.
The Skeptic identified a high-severity ranking problem sufficient to rerank, but not to abstain, because S1C41 provides a supported full-coverage alternative.

counterfactual_failures: The proposed rank-1 choice would likely change if the tackifier axis were restricted to its stated evidence-supported region; S1C41 becomes preferable to S1C40.
The lower burden of S1C40 is not a valid advantage if its 2.5% tackifier level is unsupported; this is not a fair minimum-sufficient comparison against S1C41 at 5%.
The proposal does not specify whether improvement must approach the E1 low-drift reference, so passing relative to E5 alone may not demonstrate meaningful mitigation.
A hold improvement could still be explained by realization/process-state differences unless complete process history, stoichiometric verification, and state indicators are obtained.

The experiment cannot establish whether acrylic, tackifier, or their interaction caused an effect; this is acceptable for performance mitigation, but the proposal should not use the result for causal claims.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C40 uses 2.5% minor tackifier, while get_candidate_hypothesis defines the broad supported region as 3-10% and the repeated direct-analogue cluster as 4.8-6.4%. Its lower total burden therefore reflects an unsupported extrapolation rather than minimum sufficient intervention within the supported region.
critical_findings.issue: The proposed rank-1 candidate is not within the stated evidence-supported tackifier loading region.

critical_findings.evidence: The proposer calls S1C40 a minimum-sufficient full-coverage test, but the 2.5% tackifier level is not supported by the stated candidate hypothesis. S1C41 at 5% covers both axes while remaining inside the repeated minor-resin evidence cluster.
critical_findings.issue: The minimum-burden rationale is applied before loading-level evidence sufficiency is established for the tackifier axis.

critical_findings.evidence: “Unacceptable run-to-run spread” and “non-interpretable temperature response” have no frozen numerical or operational thresholds. The criterion compares only against E5, so a candidate could pass while remaining substantially inferior to the low-drift E1 reference or while showing a tradeoff in repeatability and temperature sensitivity.
critical_findings.issue: The acceptance criteria are incomplete and partly post-hoc.

critical_findings.evidence: The candidate alters the reactive-core total by adding modifiers, while the hypothesis warns that modifier OH or other NCO-reactive functionality requires recalculation of true stoichiometry. All candidates have six missing process-history fields, and S1C41 still carries high process-history uncertainty.
critical_findings.issue: Stoichiometric and realization uncertainty remains unresolved for the selected composition.

critical_findings.evidence: The plan calls for a 120 °C anchor after equilibration and separately uses a 15-minute hold baseline, but does not explicitly define whether the anchor is the pre-hold baseline, how sampling affects the trajectory, or how calibration will avoid obscuring the absolute SI calculation.
critical_findings.issue: The state-anchor timing is insufficiently specified for separating scale calibration from temporal drift.

critical_findings.evidence: The acrylic 15% level is explicitly noncommensurate and the tackifier evidence is analogue or general guidance. These support candidate-family selection, not a local optimum or a predicted stability benefit.
critical_findings.issue: The proposal risks overstating local relevance of external analogue percentages.

interpretability_failures: S1C40's 2.5% tackifier loading is below the declared supported region, so any negative or positive result would confound chemistry testing with unsupported dose selection.
No numerical threshold is provided for acceptable repeatability, CV, maximum/minimum ratio, or temperature-response fit quality.
The plan does not explicitly predeclare how to adjudicate a candidate that improves hold drift but worsens repeatability, state sensitivity, or temperature-response behavior.
The candidate's modifier functionality and contribution to NCO:OH balance are not specified sufficiently to ensure that the intended E2 stoichiometric comparison is realized.

leakage_check.detail: The supplied tool trace states that validation formulation identity and outcome were not visible, and the candidate construction is described as pre-result. No held-out wet-lab result or outcome-derived label is evident in the payload.

regularity_alignment.detail: The proposal correctly uses the upstream finding that thermal-hold drift is distinct from static viscosity, preserves the E2 reactive-core reference, includes both independently supported axes for a performance-mitigation intent, and plans state calibration plus matched 120 °C hold measurements. However, rank-1 S1C40 uses 2.5% tackifier, which is below the stated broad supported tackifier region of 3-10% and below the repeatedly documented 4.8-6.4% cluster.

required_corrections: Replace S1C40 as performance rank-1 with S1C41 or another full-coverage candidate whose acrylic and tackifier loadings both lie within the declared evidence-supported regions; S1C41 is the most defensible supplied alternative.
Do not describe minimum sufficient intervention as established for a loading below the frozen evidence region.
Freeze numerical acceptance thresholds for repeatability, temperature-response interpretability, and acceptable tradeoffs before result inspection.
Add a prespecified comparison against the E1 low-drift reference or define why E5-relative improvement alone is sufficient.

Verify modifier functionality and recalculate NCO:OH stoichiometry before preparation, documenting all six missing process-history fields or explicitly declaring the experiment uninterpretable if they remain missing.
Define the state-anchor timing and distinguish the baseline used for SI from the anchor used for state-shift calibration.
Retain the external percentages as bounded analogue evidence only, without treating any loading as an exact local optimum.

scientific_boundary_check.detail: The proposal generally respects the boundary between local measured rheology, external analogue evidence, and conservative design rules, and it does not claim a molecular mechanism. Qualification is required because S1C40's 2.5% tackifier level is treated as a supported low-burden intervention despite falling below the stated supported loading interval.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, realization/process state primarily shifts viscosity scale while a low-complexity common thermal-response shape remains transferable.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.
